items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I asked Bob to be my guide and we took the subway... Bob showed me how to change

ctx.x: Bob Sawyer always knew where a party was taking place and sometimes I would take out my trumpet and blow with the pianist who would be engaged to put life into the shindig. Chicks were jumping, I was working and New York was like Heaven on earth for me.

Harlem was booming and I had been there 3 months before I had gone further down town than 125th Street. I had had all the enjoyment that I sought from there up to the Savoy. But one day I got the feeling to go down town and see what the centre of Manhattan was like. I asked Bob to be my guide and we took the subway from 135th Street and Lenox Avenue and came out at 42nd Street and Broadway. Broadway was the busiest Street that I had ever seen and suddenly it seemed to me that all the people in the world must be…

The tall buildings in down town Manhattan were amazing. Cincinnati had a tall building called the Skyscraper, but to me most of the buildings in down town New York were skyscrapers and the Woolworth building was almost twice as tall as the skyscraper in Cincinnati. There seemed to be thousands of movie houses and theatres. This was an Alice in Wonderland land that the Indians had sold for 25 dollars. They really were not booted.
